subject: Request: SLA carve-out for content-filter & tool-call fallbacks — Brightwell Health
messages:
From: Emma Cho <emma.cho@brightwellhealth.com>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Brightwell Health Legal <legal@brightwellhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SLA question — filtering & tool-calls

Hi Lauren,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're close to internal approval but our security and compliance teams flagged a concern: Brightwell's clinical assistant will call out to several downstream tools (medication lookup, PHI redaction, structured-output JSON for our EHR). They want clarity on how Redwood treats outages or performance degradations that are specifically caused by content-filtering triggers or tool-calling failures.

Two asks:
1) We need a carve-out or alternative SLO language that recognizes "filter-triggered response truncation" and "tool-call fallback" as a distinct class of failures for which uptime credits / remediation can be different.
2) If Redwood can't cover those in the standard SLA, can you provide a runbook and visibility (logs, timestamps) for incidents so our auditors can reconcile patient-impact windows?

Shipping this to our legal team as well — copied. Can you propose concrete wording and/or a credits table?

Best,
Emma
Emma Cho

Brightwell Health

From: lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 09:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SLA question — filtering & tool-calls

Emma — thanks for the clear ask and for looping legal. High level: we treat runtime filter activation and tool-call fallbacks as operational events that can have different remediation mechanics from core runtime outage. We can propose a carve-out that: 
- Specifies "filter-induced degradation" as any request where a content filter returns a non-empty block/rewrite that prevents expected structured output, or where tool-call choreography returns a 5xx/timeout and the runtime returns a degraded/fallback response.
- Provides limited SLA crediting: smaller credit band (e.g., 10-25% of the token/availability credit) for verified incidents caused solely by filter/tool failure vs. full service outage.

I'll put together suggested contract language and attach a proposed credits table. For logs — we can provide a timestamped incident export (filter verdict, tool-call IDs, latency) with a 90-day retention by default and extended retention for enterprise.

Cc'ing Karthik and Monica to confirm technical feasibility and to draft the SLO wording.

—Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Head of Sales, Enterprise
Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, monica_patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 11:38:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: SLA question — filtering & tool-calls

Quick tech note — from the runtime side:
- Filter activations are deterministic per model/version and our decision logs include filter_id, verdict, and token offset. We can surface those in the incident export.
- Tool-call failures are handled by the orchestration layer. We currently classify these as "dependent-service failures". For a carve-out we need to be explicit about fallback behaviors: retry window (default 500ms x 2), whether we return partial structured output, and when we consider a request successful vs. degraded.
- We can produce an "incident proof" bundle for each claim: request_id, model_version, filter_verdicts, tool_call_ids and upstream HTTP codes. That satisfies auditors.

Operational ask: legal should accept language that requires Brightwell to provide request_ids and a 30-day window to validate claims before credits are applied. Otherwise we risk over-allocating credits for edge cases.

-Karthik
Principal Product Manager, Runtime

From: Brightwell Health Legal <legal@brightwellhealth.com>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Emma Cho <emma.cho@brightwellhealth.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Nov 2026 08:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SLA question — filtering & tool-calls

Hi Lauren,

Thanks. A few items from our side:
- We need precise definitions in the agreement for:
  * "Filter-induced data suppression" (when filter prevents output that would otherwise be present)
  * "Tool-call failure" (including retries and timeouts)
- Credits must be auditable. We'll require the incident proof bundle and a maximum 45-day compliance window for Redwood to issue any credits.
- For clinical impact scenarios (where a returned output omission could affect patient safety) we require an escalation path and a dedicated POC.

Can Redwood provide a template carve-out clause and sample credit schedule?

Regards,
Clara Juarez
Counsel, Brightwell Health
legal@brightwellhealth.com

From: lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Clara Juarez <legal@brightwellhealth.com>, Emma Cho <emma.cho@brightwellhealth.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, monica_patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 10:15:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: SLA question — filtering & tool-calls (proposal attached)

Clara / Emma — attached is a proposed carve-out clause and a tiered credits schedule. Highlights:
- Definitions section with exact criteria for filter-induced suppression and tool-call failures.
- Credits: 15% token/availability credit for verified filter/tool incidents (max per month cap), 40% for "compound incidents" where a tool-call failure plus runtime degradation caused service unavailability.
- Proof bundle requirement: Brightwell must provide request_ids within 30 days; Redwood will respond within 45 days with verification and credit calculation.
- For clinical-impact incidents we agree to a joint post-incident review within 72 hours and an optional on-call rotation for the duration of the pilot.

Rishi — can you confirm we can commit to the 45-day verification window and the post-incident review SLA for pilot customers in healthcare?

—Lauren

From: rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Clara Juarez <legal@brightwellhealth.com>, Emma Cho <emma.cho@brightwellhealth.com>

Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: SLA question — filtering & tool-calls (ack & next steps)

Clara / Emma — we can commit to the verification timeline (45 days) and the 72-hour joint post-incident review for clinical-impact incidents during the contracted pilot. Operational notes:
- We'll include filter verdict exports and tool-call traces in the proof bundles. For pilots, we'll enable extended logging retention (180 days) under the enterprise addendum.
- Credits will be issued as billing adjustments applied to the next invoice after verification.

Next steps I propose:
1) Brightwell to confirm acceptance of definition language in the PDF (slo-proposal-brightwell-20261125.pdf).
2) Sign the addendum (DocuSign link shared on Monday) to enable extended logs and the pilot carve-out.
3) Kick off a 2-week run with on-call support to tune filter thresholds and retry windows.

If that works, Lauren — please share the DocuSign link and the SUP-9887 ticket so Brightwell legal can reference the operational attachment.
